identity: Engineer and university teacher · United States · 1883–1959
title: Edith Clarke's birth chart
metaDescription: Edith Clarke's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 21.7° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun and Jupiter sit 0.3° from an exact trine — near enough that the tradition reads identity and expansion as a single working part. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Aquarius, but precisely: 21.7°, third decan, 20°–30°, under Venus in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 11.5° Aquarius, Venus at 5.0° Capricorn, Mars at 6.0° Aquarius. Mercury in a air sign reads as a mind at home in argument and pattern; Venus in a earth sign reads as taste for the substantial and the lasting; Mars in a air sign reads as drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun to Jupiter is the closest call of the day, a trine within 0.3°. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, Jupiter square Uranus at 1.1°, and the Sun square Saturn at 2.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has two entries for this chart. The Sun in Aquarius at 21.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Gemini at 21.4° is in detriment. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 5 earth, 4 air by element and 6 fixed, 2 mutable, 1 cardinal by modality. No settled placement falls in fire or water — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Mercury, Jupiter, Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Pisces into Aries during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.8° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
